sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Document Automation and E-Signature Authentication

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch Common Law, English Common Law influence, statutory regulation; no Sharia law application)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment
South Africa-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement, 2019
South Africa-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (terminated effective 2024; residual protections under domestic law and applicable treaties)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 and Act 1 of 2023; Companies Act 71 of 2008 including the Beneficial Ownership provisions introduced by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2023; Companies Regulations 2011 (Regulations 22 and 23); Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) Guidance Note 4C (Beneficial Ownership Filings); Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (original or certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (DIRCO apostille for foreign use; domestic validation is internal to CIPC)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / incorporators' authorized agent, filed with CIPC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if executed abroad) or Consular Legalization (non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Resolution authorizing incorporation and appointment of first directors / initial directors' consent form (CoR 2.2)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and proposed directors; notarial attestation recommended
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (foreign signatories) or Consular Legalization (non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Schedule (CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register submission)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company's first directors or designated compliance officer; supporting identity documents of UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copies for foreign natural persons; Hague Apostille for underlying ID/passport copies; consular legalization by South African embassy or consulate for non-Hague-Party documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign shareholder due diligence pack (certified passport copies, proof of address, global sanctions/PEP questionnaire)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner, validated by a regulated South African bank or FIC accountable institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of notarial true copies; alternatively consular legalization for non-Hague-Party documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant / ultimate beneficial owner and proposed shareholders; notarized locally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization when executed outside South Africa

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening against FIC's domestic terrorism and proliferation financing lists, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN list for USD-denominated commercial ties, European Union consolidated sanctions list for EU payment rails, United Kingdom (OFSI) consolidated list, and South African targeted financial sanctions lists under POCDATARA and the Implementation of Certain International Trade Controls Measures Act (ITCMA); enhanced due diligence mandatory for any PEP, immediate family member or close associate of a PEP; electronic verification against public registers and reliable independent data sources with document retention for five years after business relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal (cservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be in any of South Africa's 11 official languages but, when used in serious commercial documentation, must be in characters that form part of the alphabet normally used by the nation; the name is not required to include an English translation, but when an abbreviation is adopted it must follow the '(Pty) Ltd' suffix (Proprietary Limited); names must not be offensive, offensive to any section of the population or contrary to public interest; the name of a foreign company doing business in South Africa that does not end with 'Proprietary Limited' will have '(South Africa)' added at the end of its name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Prohibited words requiring prior ministerial approval: 'bank', 'building society', 'insurance', 'assurance', 'unit trust', 'collective investment scheme', 'stock exchange', 'financial services provider', 'medical scheme', 'trust', 'charity', 'church', 'university', 'college', 'institute', 'municipal', 'national', 'international', 'republic', 'government', 'president', 'minister', 'sheriff', 'judge', 'magistrate', 'parliament', 'intelligence', 'defence', 'security', 'reserve bank', 'exchange control', 'auditor', 'accountant', 'attorney', 'notary', 'conveyancer', 'engineer', 'architect', 'surveyor', 'reserve', and any other token that suggests the company is an organ of state, a financial institution, a regulated profession, or an entity enjoying government-backed authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a notice of refusal, the applicant must lodge an application for name reconsideration with CIPC within 20 business days of the date of the notice of refusal, using the prescribed CoR 9.4 form or the online e-service dispute mechanism; if CIPC confirms the refusal, the applicant must within 30 days after receipt of the confirmation deliver an application to the Companies Tribunal by Form CTR 135, together with a supporting affidavit setting out the grounds for review; the Companies Tribunal may then set aside the refusal, direct CIPC to reserve the name for a further period, or impose conditions on the use of the name; alternatively the applicant may apply to the High Court for an administrative review under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000, provided the prescribed 180-day judicial review window is respected.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally accepted as the registered office for low-risk standard activities under CIPC if the address is a physical address and mail is capable of being delivered and received there; however, for a LegalTech SaaS using Stripe and credit-card rails, the registered office must be a location that can receive statutory notices and legal service; a pure desk-share or non-physical address is not acceptable; the address must not be a post office box; a professional business centre suite address will satisfy CIPC requirements, but the company must ensure that the centre accepts service of legal process and provides document-forwarding and electronic notification; for banking and FICA purposes the physical or operational presence must be verifiable, and economic substance regulations will not trigger separate CIPC requirements because the entity is a private company without a ring-fenced cross-border holding; however, for tax residency and VAT purposes the place of effective management should be in South Africa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate (quantified estimate approximately 8%–15% per operational year); CIPC and the South African Revenue Service (SARS) will not routinely conduct unannounced inspections for a newly incorporated private company, but if the company is flagged for AML risk, VAT refunds, or reportable arrangements, the likelihood of a physical verification may increase to 35%–50%; banks and payment service providers may perform periodic virtual due-diligence on-site visits as part of AML/CFT monitoring, and the FIC can require an on-site inspection under FICA where a reportable non-compliance pattern is observed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC company name reservation and incorporation filing fee including registration of MOI and first directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published by DTI/CIPC as at Financial Year 2024/2025 (ZAR 175 for standard e-filing; USD equivalent approximate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: CIPC (complimentary filing through CIPC e-Services upon incorporation; no separate statutory levy)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (nil additional fee, included in incorporation filing costs)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial certification or apostille for foreign UBO identity documents (2-4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: South African notary public (where executed abroad, local notary in foreign state; DIRCO for apostille)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document — Range ZAR 350–1,200 per notarial page plus DIRCO apostille fees (ZAR 30–60 per apostille), converted to USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service (12-month virtual office with physical street address and mail/legal process service, professional business centre)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Business centre / registered office service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and corporate secretarial retainer for pre-incorporation compliance, MOI drafting, UBO questionnaire, and AML/KYC pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Attorney and corporate secretarial advisor (external legal counsel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (professional hourly rates ZAR 1,200–3,500 per hour / fixed scope ZAR 12,000–20,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: FICA accountable institution establishment pack: bank account opening and PEP/sanctions screening (first account at commercial bank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: South African clearing bank / financial institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Banking Association of South Africa fee guidelines (monthly account fee for Business Zero or similar; first month prepayment)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC CoR 9.4 name reconsideration contingency reserve (10% likelihood of administrative review)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: CIPC (if CoR 9.4 lodged by online submission; no direct fee, but legal drafting contingency included)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administration fee (ZAR 100–200 per reconsideration / Companies Tribunal fees, converted to USD)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss. 13, 14, 15-19 (incorporation, Notice of Incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation) and s. 66 (board of directors); Companies Regulations, 2011 (GNR 351 of 26 April 2011), Forms CoR 9.1 and CoR 14.1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a National Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) agency, registration via CIPC e-Services
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. The Companies Act 71 of 2008 does not prescribe a minimum issued share capital for a private company (Pty) Ltd; shares may be issued without par value and consideration may be cash, property, or promissory notes. No escrow account or Government capital deposit is required; the MOI may define authorized share classes and transfer restrictions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company as a Proprietary Limited company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 be ratified and that the initial shares reflected in the Memorandum of Incorporation be allotted and issued to the subscribers, the agreed consideration being fully received and recorded as paid. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at [physical address in South Africa], that the postal address be recorded as [postal address], and that these particulars be filed with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [full name] be appointed as the first director and be authorized to open corporate bank accounts, appoint auditors or accounting officers as required by law, and execute all ancillary documents. CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - e-Services Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the CIPC e-Services portal with a registered brand/customer account; select the Name Reservation service; submit Form CoR 9.1 with up to three proposed company names; pay the prescribed fee online; the system applies automated screening for similarity and undesirability under section 11 of the Companies Act before approval.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 9.1
Certified copy of applicant identity document or passport
CIPC e-Services user profile and credentials
Online payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of undesirability or confusing similarity, file a fresh CoR 9.1 application with alternative names or lodge a written objection/appeal with the CIPC Commissioner within 30 days. Alternatively, proceed with incorporation using the auto-generated company registration number as the company name and apply for a name change later via Form CoR 15.1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - e-Services Portal or registered CIPC filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) together with the electronically signed MOI through the CIPC e-Services 'Company Registration' workflow; select 'Private Company' where no public offering or minimum capital applies; pay the state fee; upon successful verification the CIPC system issues the company registration number (e.g. 202X/XXXXXX/07) and the Certificate of Incorporation is made available for download as a verified digital document.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 14.1
Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) in prescribed form
Certified copies of directors' identity documents or passports
Valid CIPC name reservation reference (if name reserved)
Notarially certified power of attorney if filed through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected for data errors or MOI non-compliance with sections 15-17, cure the matter through the CIPC e-Services correction workflow within 21 days; amend and re-submit the relevant schedules. Any third-party objection to the incorporation is adjudicated by the CIPC registrar prior to issuance of the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation First Board Meeting and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company / registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting within seven days of incorporation; adopt the First Board Resolution covering share allotment, confirmation of the registered office, appointment of the initial director, and banking mandates; issue share certificates; open the securities register and statutory minute book; retain the consent-to-act forms of directors at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution
Share certificates issued to subscribers
Securities register / share register
Memorandum of Incorporation
Directors' consent to act forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Not applicable - internal corporate act; any defect is curable by a unanimous board or shareholder resolution and supporting written consent records, without CIPC involvement unless the MOI or filed particulars require amendment via Form CoR 15.1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the South African Revenue Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - eFiling Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company on SARS eFiling using the CIPC registration number; complete the IT010 income tax registration; apply for VAT (VAT101) if annual turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed ZAR 1 million; register for PAYE, SDL and UIF once the first employee is appointed; obtain the tax reference number and verify tax clearance status through the SARS Tax Clearance Status system.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation and registration number
Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified identity documents and residential address of directors
Bank account confirmation details
SARS eFiling account credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration due to mismatched director or address data, correct the error via eFiling 'Request Correction' or attend a SARS branch appointment with certified supporting documents; disputed assessments or registrations may be challenged under section 103 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Information Regulator (South Africa) - online registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Given the LegalTech data processing scope, register the appointed Information Officer with the Information Regulator as required by regulation 4(2)(d) of the POPIA Regulations; complete the online registration form identifying the company as a responsible party; upload the appointment and consent documents so the company is listed on the Regulator's public register of Information Officers.
required_dossiers: Completed POPIA Information Officer Registration form
Written appointment letter of the Information Officer and any deputies
CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Signed consent of the Information Officer to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is rejected for incomplete particulars, re-submit through the Information Regulator online portal with a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation and corrected appointment letter; no appeal fee applies and the Regulator may be contacted directly for technical rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational, Fire and Physical Premises Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (Compensation Fund and UIF); local municipal fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon commencement of operations from physical premises, obtain a Certificate of Occupancy / Completion Certificate for the leased office; procure a Fire Safety Certificate from the local municipal fire service confirming compliance with SANS 10400 and the National Building Regulations; register with the Compensation Fund (Form W.As.2) and the Unemployment Insurance Fund for COIDA and UIF compliance before the first employee commences duties.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and Certificate of Occupancy
Fire safety inspection checklist and municipal fire certificate
Form W.As.2 COIDA employer registration
UIF employer registration
OHS Act compliance audit report and health and safety representative appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late COIDA/UIF registration attracts penalties; remedy by submitting an affidavit explaining the timeline and completing registration at the local Labour Centre. If the fire certificate is suspended, implement the municipal compliance notice, rectify the stated deficiencies, and request re-inspection within the stipulated period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral licensing authority for ISIC 6201 software activities under South African law; the Information Regulator (South Africa) supervises mandatory POPIA Information Officer registration, while the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) retains residual policy oversight
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industry-specific operating license required for cloud document automation e-signature LegalTech SaaS; mandatory statutory registration is the POPIA Information Officer Registration (s. 55, Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based software activities are not listed under Listing Notices 1, 2 or 3 of the EIA Regulations, 2014 (GNR 982/983/984); no environmental authorization or basic assessment is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge generated; sanitary effluent complies with municipal sewer discharge limits under the National Water Act 36 of 1998; waste shall be disposed via registered municipal and e-waste recyclers in accordance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008; office noise and air emissions subject only to local municipal by-laws and general air quality norms under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the local municipal fire service under SANS 10400 and the Fire Brigade Services Act 99 of 1987; structural Certification of Occupancy for the leased premises; Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 workplace audit, appointment of a health and safety representative, and COIDA registration with the Compensation Fund evidenced by a Letter of Good Standing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); portal: SARS eFiling at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; corporate registry interface: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) at https://www.cipc.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated (Pty) Ltd is auto-registered with SARS for Income Tax upon CIPC incorporation and receives an income tax reference number. The company must then: (1) appoint a South African-resident public officer within one month of incorporation and register the appointment with SARS; (2) register for VAT via SARS eFiling within 21 days after the end of the month in which taxable turnover exceeds or is likely to exceed ZAR 1,500,000, or voluntarily where turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000; (3) register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and SDL before making payments to employees; (4) obtain a customs importer/exporter code if cross-border goods movement occurs; and (5) declare non-resident director/shareholder particulars and ultimate beneficial ownership to CIPC and SARS. Foreign companies establishing a branch or having a place of effective management in South Africa must obtain a SARS tax reference number for the branch. Tax registration is confirmed through the SARS eFiling profile and a tax compliance status certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (residence-based): a (Pty) Ltd is a separate legal taxpayer subject to corporate income tax at 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident companies are taxed on South African-source income; there is no pass-through or check-the-box election; distributions are subject to 20% dividends tax; a foreign company branch is taxed at 27% on South African-source income with no separate remittance tax; the entity is not situated in a tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; a (Pty) Ltd is per se a taxable entity. Available elections and special regimes include: (i) Headquarters Company election under s 9I of the Income Tax Act granting conduit treatment for qualifying foreign dividends, interest, royalties and disposal gains, subject to prescribed non-resident shareholding, foreign group income and expense/asset composition thresholds; (ii) Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) attribution elections and foreign business establishment exemptions under s 9D; (iii) VAT grouping application under s 50(2) VAT Act to treat related persons as a single vendor; (iv) VAT cash-basis election under s 15(2A) VAT Act for vendors with taxable turnover not exceeding ZAR 2,500,000; (v) Small Business Corporation progressive rate election under s 12E for qualifying companies with turnover below ZAR 20,000,000; (vi) foreign exchange rate valuation elections under s 24I; and (vii) s 11D R&D allowance election subject to Department of Science and Innovation pre-approval. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are adjusted mandatorily under ss 8E, 8EA, 8F and 23M, with no elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) governed by the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991; nationally administered by SARS with no sub-national sales tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,500,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period (threshold raised from ZAR 1,000,000 effective 1 April 2024); voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000; foreign suppliers of electronic services must register for VAT when electronic services exceed ZAR 50,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or national e-invoicing API is currently in force as at 2025. SARS operates a phased e-invoicing framework through the SARS Digital Gateway (secure PDF/XML with integrity hash) and has announced incremental mandates, but the existing statutory obligations are: registered vendors must issue a s 20 VAT tax invoice within 21 days of the date of supply, retain records for 5 years, and file VAT201 returns electronically via SARS eFiling on a monthly or bi-monthly basis as allocated by SARS; high-volume filers may be required to submit via SARS API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (1) exports of movable goods physically removed from South Africa within 90 days of supply where the vendor retains documentary proof (s 11(1)(a) and (b) VAT Act); and (2) exported services supplied to a non-resident who is outside South Africa at the time the services are rendered and who does not consume or use the services in South Africa (s 11(2)(l) VAT Act). For LegalTech SaaS and e-signature automation services, the supplier must verify the foreign status of the recipient and the absence of local use/consumption. Services supplied in connection with land or movable property situated in South Africa at the time of supply, or services physically rendered in South Africa, do not qualify. All zero-rated invoices must be annotated with the applicable zero-rating reason and supported by export evidence retained before the VAT return is filed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) electronically lodged with SARS Customs
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / road manifest evidencing physical removal of goods from South Africa
Commercial invoice annotated 'zero-rated export' showing full value, consignee, currency and applicable ISIC/code
Inward remittance evidence (SWIFT MT103 or Authorised Dealer certificate) proving actual receipt of foreign currency
For services: signed export services agreement and non-resident consumption declaration (s 11(2)(l)) supported by evidence of foreign IP/hosting and client location
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may reopen assessments within the statutory prescription period (generally 3 years, extended to 5 years for non-disclosure, and unlimited for fraud or misrepresentation) and retrospectively reinstate 15% output VAT where export status or documentary proof is deficient; the vendor bears the burden of proof. Under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, understatement penalties based on conduct apply to the VAT shortfall: standard case 10%, substantial understatement 25%, failure to take reasonable care 50%, unreasonable tax position 75%, and intentional tax evasion 150%, plus interest at the prescribed rate from the original due date. Additional non-compliance penalties and criminal prosecution for tax evasion under s 235 TAA may result in fines and imprisonment; directors or persons knowingly involved in false zero-rating declarations are jointly and severally liable, and SARS may suspend eFiling facilities and set off refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), administers exchange control under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 9 of 1933, its subordinate Notices and the Currency and Exchanges Manual, and has delegated daily execution and approval powers to Authorised Dealers (registered Tier-1 commercial banks). The Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) concurrently supervises AML/CFT compliance and reporting under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (as amended by the FIC Amendment Act 1 of 2017), including beneficial-ownership verification for corporate accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a liberalised current account alongside a managed capital account. The ZAR is effectively convertible for current-account receipts and payments (subscription fees, professional services, royalties and trade finance) provided each transaction is routed through an Authorised Dealer with an underlying invoice or contract, a proper FICA file and the standard payment-purpose declaration; no FinSurv pre-approval is needed for most current transactions below the dealer delegation ceiling (circa ZAR 10 million per service counterparty per year). Capital-account entries are more restrictive: non-resident equity investment inbound is freely permitted without SARB pre-approval, but outbound capital movements, foreign loans by residents, loop structures, round-tripping of local ZAR and offshore treasury retention require prior FinSurv authority or an Authorised-Dealer permit. Profit remittance hurdles for a non-resident shareholder of a LegalTech SaaS (Pty) Ltd are: demonstrated source of funds, CIPC beneficial-ownership coherence, a valid SARS registration and tax compliance status, and compliance with the 20% dividends tax (or applicable double-taxation treaty relief) at source; once these are met, dividends and capital proceeds are remittable without exchange-control ceilings. Net assessment: current-account convertibility is High, capital-account convertibility is Conditional and documentary.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For export of services (including SaaS, e-signature and cloud document automation), the exporter must obtain payment of the full invoice value within 180 calendar days from the date of service provision, and must surrender every foreign-currency receipt to an Authorised Dealer within 30 days of its receipt, meaning sale of the foreign currency against ZAR into the company domestic operational account at the prevailing dealer spot rate. There is no statutory partial-conversion ratio: the default legal posture is a 100% surrender obligation. The exporter may instead apply through the Authorised Dealer for permission to retain foreign currency in a designated Foreign-Currency Account (typically a discretionary retention cap of approximately ZAR 5 million equivalent), keeping the remainder due for immediate surrender; retention is granted only for genuine trade hedging or import cover and remains subject to the 180-day receipt discipline. Non-surrender, late receipt or parking of proceeds offshore is treated as unlawful externalisation under section 9 of the Currency and Exchanges Act, exposing the entity to administrative penalties, adverse FIC suspicious-transaction reporting and banking de-platforming.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (ZAR Business Current) with a linked Authorised-Dealer Foreign-Currency Account (USD/GBP/EUR) and Capital Escrow variant available for investor funds

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First National Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (FNB Business Current) with GlobalOne cross-border collections and e-series digital onboarding capable of receiving SWIFT MT103 settlement
Operational Account (BusinessZ solution) plus Capital Escrow / Trust Account product for pre-seed or vendor holdback arrangements
Operational Account (Nedbank Business Transactional) paired with the Nedbank Trade desk for LC/guarantee instruments; adequate multi-currency support

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Companies Act 2008, section 33(4)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), e-Services portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Prescribed CIPC late-filing penalty per outstanding annual return; persistent non-filing for two or more successive years may trigger administrative strike-off or deregistration under Companies Act 2008, section 82(5), with loss of legal capacity to trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and mandatory audit or independent review outcome under Companies Act 2008, section 30 and Companies Regulations 28
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Prepared for shareholders and board; retained in company records; filed with CIPC only where prescribed, including instances where the annual return or a regulator requires financial statement disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual Financial Statements must be prepared and delivered within 6 months after the financial year-end; audit or independent review must be completed before delivery
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the AFS preparation and distribution mandate is a statutory contravention; CIPC or affected shareholders may compel compliance, and the annual return may be rejected where financial disclosure is required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership annual confirmation and declaration under Companies Act 2008, section 56, as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 2022
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), beneficial ownership filing module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation submitted with, or in support of, the annual return; any change in beneficial ownership, including a share transfer changing control or entitlement, must be filed with CIPC within 7 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the beneficial ownership declaration may result in administrative penalties, adverse CIPC compliance status, and possible deregistration referral; knowingly submitting false information may attract criminal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Public Interest Score determination and supporting records under Companies Regulations 26 and 28
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; the score is used by the independent reviewer or auditor and must be available to CIPC for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Computed as at each financial year-end and documented before finalising the audit or independent review scope
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An incorrect Public Interest Score may invalidate an audit exemption or review classification, requiring corrected filings and possible CIPC penalty assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A proprietary limited company must obtain a full independent audit if its Public Interest Score for the relevant financial year is 500 or more. A Public Interest Score of 100 to 499 requires an independent review unless a full audit is required by the company's Memorandum of Incorporation, shareholders, or a regulatory authority. A Public Interest Score below 100 does not require an audit or independent review, but annual financial statements must still comply with the applicable financial reporting framework if prepared.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or IFRS for SMEs as adopted by the South African Accounting Standards Board; a private (Pty) Ltd without public accountability normally applies IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CIPC requires the beneficial ownership register to be filed and confirmed as part of the annual return cycle. Each substantial shareholding transfer or any change to the identity of a beneficial owner must be recorded in the company's Beneficial Ownership Register and lodged with CIPC within 7 days. Directors must take reasonable steps to identify every beneficial owner, obtain the prescribed information, keep the register available for inspection, and include an accurate board-approved annual confirmation with the CIPC filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150 - US$600 per annum for a registered physical office address, CIPC liaison, and company compliance agent; market range varies by provider and service scope.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,200 - US$4,500 per annum for a low-risk proprietary limited technology entity requiring an independent review or small-company audit; a full statutory audit for a Public Interest Score of 500 or more may exceed this range.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; prior 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward; set-off in any one year capped at 75% of taxable income before loss set-off (years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022)
